prompt: My new isolation2 test lives in contrib/zdb/regress and drops a ZDB table, then does `select count(*) from zdb_get_metainfo_for_file(...)` (and similarly for zdb_get_metainfo_for_drop_flag/zdb_get_metainfo_for_visimap) to assert the metadata was cleaned up. It passes alone but goes flaky when run as part of the full schedule alongside other tests. Why, and how should I fix the query?

answer_points: These FDB-introspection UDFs (zdb_get_metainfo_for_file, zdb_get_metainfo_for_drop_flag, zdb_get_metainfo_for_visimap, etc.) return global FDB keys by default, not scoped to the current test's table
A bare count(*) mixes in tombstone/segfile/visimap keys left behind by other tests in the same schedule/cluster/FDB instance
Fix: capture the test table's relfilenode into a temp table before the DROP, then JOIN every FDB-introspection query on that relfilenode
pg_catalog.zdb_* catalog tables (e.g. zdb_backup_gc_records, zdb_shard_stats) have the same global-scope problem and must also be filtered by relfilenode
contrib/zdb/regress/sql/backup_and_gc/setup_backup.sql is a reference example of this relfilenode-join pattern
gotcha_points: did NOT use a bare count(*) without filtering by relfilenode
did NOT assume these introspection UDFs are already scoped to the caller's table
